title: Validation of the German Version of the Alexithymia Questionnaire for Children (AQC) in a Clinical Sample
summary: The difficulty of recognizing and describing one’s own feelings will be studied in children and adolescents receiving treatment in a clinic (inpatient, partial inpatient, or outpatient). For this, the Alexithymia Questionnaire for Children (AQC), which is already used in the clinic for diagnostics, will be applied. Children aged 6 and older will fill out the questionnaire themselves, and parents will also complete the same questionnaire for their child. To understand the results better, other questionnaires will also be used: the BDI-II to measure depressive symptoms in adolescents aged 13 and older, and the CBCL to assess the child's behavior (like anxiety or outbursts of anger) as reported by the parents. In addition, demographic information like age, gender, and socioeconomic status (such as parents' education level and the size of the family's hometown) will be collected to help better understand the results.

interventions.name: Data from patients aged 6 years and older who received inpatient, partial inpatient, or outpatient treatment and completed the Questionnaire for Alexithymia in Childhood and Adolescence (AQC) as part of the diagnostic process, as well as data from their parents, are being retrospectively analyzed.
